10.description: As a system administrator, I want to be able to set up a configurable cost estimate structure for each of the lifecycle stages set out in Table A of Scope.
10.acceptanceCriteria:
• An Administrator, following receipt of an RfE, can establish in the software a long-term assessment OMR estimate to satisfy the relevant lifecycle stages set out in Table A of the Scope

• Each lifecycle stage shall have one WBS configured for that stage

• Different cost plans for a scheme can be prepared by structuring an estimate by location (e.g. Segment), asset, work package/Supplier

11.description: As an estimator, I want to be able to select the time period which is to be covered by the estimate (user-configurable period, e.g. 60 / 100 / 150 years, the "assessment period")
11.acceptanceCriteria:
• A User can produce an OMR estimate for an assessment period of 1 to 200 years. The assessment period will be specified by the Project Team in the RfE

• A User can amend this assessment period if required after the estimate inception meeting

13.description: As an Estimator, I want all estimates to follow a consistent structure as set out by the MP CESS as follows: Base Estimate, Risk / Opportunity / Uncertainty (at Project, Programme and Portfolio Levels), Expenditure Profiling and Inflation.
13.acceptanceCriteria:
• A CCET User can produce the estimate using the relevant shell for the O&M and Asset Renewal components of the OMR estimate

• The OMR shell(s)shall be consistent with National Highways CESS, which will include Base, Risk/Opportunity (Project, Programme/Portfolio Level)

• The WBS for long-term appraisal OMR estimates will be consistent with the WBS for standalone O&M and Asset Renewals estimates at the upper levels of the Work Breakdown Structure (e.g., CESS heading)

• A CCET User can finalise each estimate part of a whole lifecycle cost estimate (i.e. CAPEX, OMR and combined) in Real Terms and then apply an inflation profile(s), which are stored in the software library, to produce estimates in Nominal Terms

20.description: Assign one or more cost plans (estimate type in Table A of Scope) for each lifecycle to a Scheme - Covered by FR 10
20.acceptanceCriteria: Administrators can edit a library of ‘Estimate Output Types’ that states the lifecycle stages which the Estimate Shell covers for a selected Estimate Output Type.

60.description: Request for estimate should include field for users to type in purpose of estimate.
60.acceptanceCriteria:
• As a CCET user, I can access the Estimate Request interface so that I can submit estimate requests.
• As a CCET user, I can enter the Purpose of Estimate in a free-text field so that the reviewer knows the purpose of request.

70.description: Software should allow estimators to assign "Project Users" to any type of the estimates identified in FR 10 (see Scope Table A for definition of users and estimates).
70.acceptanceCriteria:
• As an Estimating Manager / Estimating Administrator with relevant permission, I can approve requests so that estimates are initiated in the software.
• As an Estimating Manager / Estimating Administrator with relevant permission, I can assign estimators / reviewers to approved requests so that the estimate can be worked on and progressed.
• Software notifies assigned estimator and requestor when a request is approved, and estimate is initiated.

80.description: Software should show all estimates and IFT revisions for FR 10 above to administrators, only the estimates and IFT assigned to estimators and only IFT(Cost and Carbon) / IFT(Cost and Carbon) revisions assigned to the project user(Designer/PM/Contractor). This will reduce the list to navigate and will only show what is available in the system for estimator and project user(Designer/PM/Contractor).
80.acceptanceCriteria: The CCET will have an Estimate Browser that shows all National Highways estimates in the system for all lifecycle stages, subject to a user's permissions.

90.description: As a user I want to be able to identify an estimate as belonging to the "do-something" or the "do-minimum" scenario.
90.acceptanceCriteria:
• As a CCET user, I can select a ‘Scenario’ when submitting estimate requests so that I can specify if the request is for a ‘with scheme’ or ‘without scheme’ type estimate.
• As a CCET user, I can see the ‘Scenario’ of the estimate after the estimate is initiated

110.description: As an estimating manager, I want to have a logical coding for each item of works (MP, M&R and AR) that can be configured to a standard WBS for the lifecycle stage.
110.acceptanceCriteria: Each Item library will have an editable field for Item Code.

120.description: Software to allow an estimate to be requested (submit a request) via RFE for estimate types in FR 10, which is then reviewed and confirmed by Estimating manager, similar to MP.
120.acceptanceCriteria:
• As a CCET user, I can access the Estimate Request interface so that I can request any estimate type covered in scope, see Table A for definition of users and estimates.
• As a CCET user, I can submit requests so that they are stored in a central repository (portal).
• As an Estimating Manager / Estimating Administrator with relevant permission, I can access a repository / request portal so that I can review submitted estimate requests.
• As an Estimating Manager / Estimating Administrator with relevant permission, I can ask for changes so that the requestor can action changes and re-submit the request.
• As an Estimating Manager / Estimating Administrator with relevant permission, I can provide justification and reject requests so that the requestor understands the reason for rejection.
• As an Estimating Manager / Estimating Administrator with relevant permission, I can approve requests so that estimates are initiated in the software.
• As an Estimating Manager / Estimating Administrator with relevant permission, I can assign estimators / reviewers to approved requests so that the estimate initiation can proceed.
• As an Estimating Manager / Estimating Administrator with relevant permission, I can add comments while approving requests so that the assigned estimator can view my comments/notes.

130.description: Unique identifier for estimates in FR 10
130.acceptanceCriteria: Each Estimate in the CCET has a unique Estimate Identification Number.

140.description:
Client estimator should be able to take the contractor's estimate and convert this to a range estimate

 Applies to all estimate types in FR 10 Client Estimators use the Interim cost and carbon estimate revisions(preferred nominated by project users) produced by project users(Designers, PM, Contractors, etc)
140.acceptanceCriteria:
For all estimate types in FR10, an NH Estimator, with permissions to access a given Project and/or Projects, can export a nominated Project User's forecast BoQ to MS Excel and import this to a NH Estimate to form the basis of a formal NH range estimate.

For all estimate types in FR10, an NH Estimator, with permissions to access a given Project and/or Projects, can export a nominated Project User's forecast risk register to MS Excel and import this to a NH Estimate to form the basis of a formal NH range estimate.

For all estimate types in FR10, an NH Estimator, with permissions to access a given Project and/or Projects, can export a nominated Project User's forecast milestone dates and expenditure profile to MS Excel and import this to a NH Estimate to form the basis of a formal NH range estimate.

150.description: Software should allow multiple price base selection across Cost elements under segments with choice allowing inflation profile to be applied or not applied (i.e. outturn)
150.acceptanceCriteria:
• An estimator can apply multiple rate libraries to the Items in an estimate and the libraries can be at multiple price bases. Upon allocation of the rate from the library to an estimate, the rate shall be rebased in the estimate to a common price base for the estimate that is selected by the Estimator. Therefore, an estimate can use source rates that have a different price base at Item cost element level and apply any expenditure and inflation profile from the library to that Item.

• Where required at cost element level Estimator can select the Item cost element and identify/mark it as Outturn, so no inflation calculations are applied at Item cost element level, whilst still having the ability to forecast the expenditure using an expenditure profile from the library.

• A User has the flexibility to produce OMR estimates in multiple configurable formats

• The software will store multiple inflation, discounting and market adjustment factors within the library for use in OMR estimates

• An Administrator can update the stored data in the software library

• A User can apply a stored inflation profile from the software library, to the unit rate data from the software rate library, to adjust the rates to a common price base

• A User can apply a stored inflation profile from the software library, to the estimated OMR costs at a common price base to produce the outturn costs (i.e. inclusive of future inflation)

• For use in economic appraisal a User can produce estimated outputs in the following formats:

          • In real and nominal terms

          • Pre- and Post-discounting

           Pre- and Post-market adjustment factors

160.description: Software must generate an automated release email with links to the estimate outputs from data stored in estimate data base for the estimate being released. This should include, form 300, Economic output sheet, Water fall diagram, CESS, etc as per NH formal estimate release including links to IFT and Dashboards for the project.
160.acceptanceCriteria:
• As an Estimating Administrator, I can setup and maintain a release email template so that relevant email content is sent out with issued estimates.
• As an Estimating Administrator, I can setup and maintain separate ‘mandatory’ and ‘optional’ checklists for deliverables/outputs for each estimate type so that the complete release pack is available for issued estimates.
• As an estimator, I can provide custom deliverables so that issued estimates can have additional information.
• As an estimator, I can modify the auto-generated release email text so that I have the required flexibility.
• Release email contains SharePoint links to the documentation folder that contains the estimate outputs.

170.description: As an estimating manager, I want the system to produce an Estimate Approval Form, similar to the existing MP CE300 form for each estimate in Scope Table A.
170.acceptanceCriteria:
• Software generates estimate approval form (CE300) automatically on estimate approval for estimate types in FR10.
• CE300 form will be specific to estimate types in FR10.
• CE300 forms can be exported to PDF.

180.description:
Linked to FR 160, the software should create standard folder structure in the database/cloud where respective data is stored.

EMs rather than sending attachment can send links to the files stored in database/cloud specific to the estimate.
180.acceptanceCriteria:
• Software creates a standard documentation folder after an estimate request is approved and the estimate is initiated.

• As an Estimating Manager / Estimating Administrator with relevant permission, I can include links to documents in the folders stored in software database/cloud specific to the estimate.
• As an Estimating Manager / Estimating Administrator with relevant permission, I can send links to documents in the folders stored in software database/cloud to project specific users.

190.description: This is not created in the software, it is produced outside the software, however the AAS document needs to be included with the automated release email from software and stored in estimate database/cloud.
190.acceptanceCriteria:
• As an Estimating Administrator, I can setup and maintain separate ‘mandatory’ and ‘optional’ checklists for deliverables/outputs for each estimate type so that the complete release pack is available for issued estimates to release with the estimate.
• As an estimator, I can provide custom deliverables such as AAS documents to be stored in the estimate database / cloud, which are included in the release email for release of approved estimates to requestors. so that rating information is available for issued estimates.

210.description: The estimate approval form for all estimate types set out in Scope Table A should allow tables and graphics to be included on the completed Estimate Approval Form.
210.acceptanceCriteria:
• Software generates release forms (CE300) automatically on estimate approval for estimate types in FR10.
• CE300 form will be specific to estimate types in FR10 and will include the lifecycle stage - New Construction, M&R, AR.
• CE300 form includes images, graphs and tables.
• CE300 forms can be exported to PDF.

220.description: Generate Economic assessment report with each Forecast. This needs to be updated in real time.
220.acceptanceCriteria:
A CCET user can generate a report of the net present value of the forecast's costs by deflating the forecast's outturn costs for each year by a GDP deflator index stored in a library (administrator controlled). The report shall be consistent with the existing "Adjusted Economic Output" worksheet layout in NH file Interim Forecasting Tool v1.7 and exclude costs denoted as historic / sunk costs and taxation.

IFT revision and/ or revisions in CCET for all FR10 estimate types include an Economic Output(EO) calculation within the IFT revision screen, using the same format and principles as the MP CAPEX IFT revision. This EO screen in CCET is updated in real time in IFT revision.

The Economic Output report shows the net present value of forecast costs, adjusting each year's outturn costs using a GDP deflator index managed in an admin-controlled library. It matches the layout of the "Adjusted Economic Output" worksheet in NH’s Interim Forecasting Tool v1.7 and excludes historic/sunk costs and taxation.

The Economic Assessment Output can be exported to a report in Excel and PDF format

230.description: Software should produce, a CESS, RET , SAS, Form 300,ect for Asset renewal estimates in FR 10 along with the Dashboards at resource, project, Asset Class, Region and Area level, portfolio level, etc
230.acceptanceCriteria:
• The software produces fixed estimate outputs for each lifecycle cost stage and Whole Life cycle estimate for Asset renewals in FR 10, which include the below:
• A cost estimate summary at Section level, showing base estimate at Section level, project and portfolio risk/opportunity/uncertainty allowances and inflation.
• A summary of the estimated costs over time, broken down by Section level, base estimate, project risk, portfolio risk and inflation allowances for each financial year
• A summary of estimated costs for net present value calculations at an administrator-controlled price base, which:
• can be configured to exclude spend to date and taxation
• presents costs with and without portfolio risk allowances

For Form 300 see Acceptance Criteria 170.

240.description: Software should produce a CDF/PDF for cost estimates rather than the mathematically calculated and produced graph in RET. It should do for all types of estimate in FR 10.
240.acceptanceCriteria:
• The software displays a cumulative distribution function (CDF) chart on screen for a probabilistic cost estimate output
• The CDF chart can be exported as a PDF or Excel report with the chart and data table of percentile values
• The software produces a probability distribution function (PDF) chart on screen for a probabilistic cost estimate output
• The PDF chart can be exported as a PDF or Excel report with the chart and data table of percentile values
• The graphs generated should be fed directly from the cached simulation data for that project where a full Monte Carlo simulation has been run
• Users can identify the project name(s), estimates name(s) and estimate ID(s) within the reports
• The data displays identical numbers to the estimate database
• The data should be shown on one single page

250.description: An expenditure output report ("SAS") should be produced, similar to the existing Forecast format, for each interim forecast produced from an estimate (for all estimate types as per Scope Table A).
250.acceptanceCriteria:
A CCET user can generate a report of historic costs and forecast costs by year by Section and Cost Element, similar to the existing "Adjusted SAS Output" worksheet layout in NH file Interim Forecasting Tool v1.7 .

IFT revision and/ or revisions in CCET for all FR10 estimate types includes a SAS Output screen and output report similar to the existing "Adjusted SAS Output" worksheet layout in NH file Interim Forecasting Tool v1.7. The generated IFT revision screen / report includes historic costs and forecast costs by year/months by Section and Cost Element. Sections and Cost elements vary differ for each estimate type in FR10 and includes, forecast of fee, risks / opportunities / uncertainties, inflation, portfolio risks, etc

260.description: The software should produce carbon reports at each level of the WBS (for all estimates types as per Scope Table A) from resource to portfolio level, across PAS2080 modules and by expenditure period.
260.acceptanceCriteria:
• A report of estimated carbon can be produced for each estimate type, displaying estimated carbon impact:
   • By PAS 2080 module
   • By Resource
   • By Item
   • By Section
   • By Time period
• A report of estimated carbon can be produced for a programme, displaying estimated carbon impact:
   • By PAS 2080 module
   •  By Project
   • By Time period
• A report of estimated carbon can be produced for a portfolio, displaying estimated carbon impact:
   • By PAS 2080 module
   • By Programme
   • By Time period
• The reports can be export to PDF and Excel format
• Users can identify the project name(s), estimates name(s) and estimate ID(s) within the reports
• The data displays identical numbers to the estimate database

262.description: For estimates that are for standalone schemes / M&R contracts (over shorter timescales, e.g. less than 10 years) expenditure profiles should be available by month.  For longer term estimates required for whole life cost over longer assessment periods (e.g. 60 years) expenditure data should be available by year.
262.acceptanceCriteria: Administrators can store and edit default expenditure profiles for Operation and Maintenance works in an Expenditure Profile library.

263.description: As an estimator, I want to be able to see the expenditure profile for an estimate easily using the same User interface as for estimate production, i.e. not have to leave the estimate production module in order to view the estimated expenditure profile. For example, PowerBI dashboards or PDF reports are not a replacement for user interface / screens presenting this information in the estimating module itself.
263.acceptanceCriteria: As an estimator or estimating manager I am able to directly access the cost and carbon expenditure profile for the estimate from the main estimate build-up screen.

270.description: Generate Cost and Carbon reports by Resource Group, Resource Category, etc.
270.acceptanceCriteria:
• A report of estimated carbon can be produced for each estimate type, displaying estimated carbon impact:
   • By Resource Group
   • By Resource Category
• A report of estimated carbon can be produced at programme level, displaying estimated carbon impact:
   • By Resource Group
   • By Resource Category
• A report of estimated carbon can be produced at portfolio level, displaying estimated carbon impact:
   • By Resource Group
   • By Resource Category
• The reports can be export to PDF and Excel format
• Users can identify the project name(s), estimates name(s) and estimate ID(s) within the reports
• The data displays identical numbers to the estimate database

280.description: As an estimator, I want to be able to see the cost and carbon outputs for an estimate easily using the same User interface as for estimate production, i.e. not have to leave the estimate production module in order to view the outputs. For example, PowerBI dashboards or PDF reports are not a replacement for user interface / screens presenting this information in the estimating module itself.
280.acceptanceCriteria: • The outputs(report & dashboards) for an approved estimate are visible on screen within the same user interface screens as the estimate production.

290.description: Generate Cost and Carbon reports inclusive and exclusive of Programme and Portfolio Risk
290.acceptanceCriteria:
• For all reports that include programme / portfolio risk allowances, the user can generate a report with or without programme / portfolio risk allowances
• All relevant reports should clearly state whether programme / portfolio risk allowances are included or excluded from the reported values

300.description: As an estimator, I want to be able to see the cost and carbon outputs for an estimate easily using the same User interface as for estimate production, i.e. not have to leave the estimate production module in order to view the outputs. For example, PowerBI dashboards or PDF reports are not a replacement for user interface / screens presenting this information in the estimating module itself.
300.acceptanceCriteria: • The outputs for an approved estimate are visible on screen within the estimating software system.

310.description: Dashboards and PDF reports should be configurable to select, resource, scheme, package, asset class, region, area or portfolio.
310.acceptanceCriteria:
• An interactive ‘dashboard’ or dashboards can be displayed on screen for a cost estimate, able to display estimated costs and carbon as follows:
   • By Resource
   • By Item
   • By Section
   • By Asset class
   • By Location
   • By Time period
• Dashboards can be displayed on screen for a collection of selected cost estimates comprising a programme, with aggregated costs and carbon for each selected estimate displaying:
   • Key Resources by value
   • Key Items by value
   • By Section
   • By Project
   • By Asset class
   • By Location
   • By Time period

320.description: View the estimated expenditure profile and dashboards and PDF reports by cost element, by time period and see costs inclusive and exclusive of risk for each time period, similar to the existing "SAS" report.
320.acceptanceCriteria:
• For each estimate type, a user can generate a report of estimated cost and carbon expenditure over the duration of expenditure displaying the following for each year within the expenditure duration:
   • Base estimate for each Section (at the base estimate price base)
   • Project Risk for each Section (at the base estimate price base)
   • Programme / Portfolio Risk (at the base estimate price base)
   • Inflation (at the base estimate price base)
• A user can generate reports including and excluding programme / portfolio risk
• The reports can be displayed on screen
• The reports can be exported to PDF.

340.description: The software shall produce cost and carbon reports for all estimates to ICMS, with granularity aligned with PAS 2080.
340.acceptanceCriteria: The Estimator can edit a data field for each Item in an estimate and enter an ICMS code reference in this field.

350.description: Software should a) allow Carbon Reduction Targets (CAP) to be ingested into the system, it should than be used by the software to show in reports and Dashboards comparison between. Baseline and CAP, from IFT revision carbon against CAP and Baseline. This should apply for all estimate types in FR 10. Reports shall be produced for aggregated estimates /caps for Programme and Portfolio level reports.
350.acceptanceCriteria:
• An authorised user can enter a Carbon Reduction Targets for a project in the software
• A user can see a report or dashboard that compares the Carbon Reduction Targets with an estimate for the project
• I should also be able to see a reports showing the aggregated latest estimate data versus the aggregated carbon reduction targets at Programme or Portfolio Level
• The data is based on approved estimates only and informed by either the preferred estimates or reference estimates (tbc by the client)
• As a user I can see how a forecast submitted by a Project User compares to the Carbon Reduction Target (CAP) for that project

360.description: Software should allow actual cost data to be incrementally ingested into the software at the estimates granularity level and allow comparison to be made between any estimate and the Actual cost(Final cost compare with all estimates on the scheme). Applies to all estimates in FR 10.
360.acceptanceCriteria:
• A user can upload actual cost data for a completed project, to a ‘Final Cost’ shell for the project
• The ‘Final Cost’ shell structure will align with the levels of the WBS at which the estimate is produced for the corresponding estimate type in FR10.
• A user can generate a comparison between the ‘Final Cost’ and an earlier estimate for the project, on screen in the software
• The dashboards can be export to PDF and Excel format
• Users can identify the project name, estimates names and estimate IDs within the comparison report
• The data displays identical numbers to the estimate database

370.description: The interim forecasting for all estimate types as per Scope table A, should produce a report for export to cost management software at Cost Element level.
370.acceptanceCriteria:
• A user can select a forecast submitted by a Project User and generate a report to MS Excel format of aggregated estimated costs for the project structured by assigned cost management codes at Cost element level.
• This report will be a fixed report, controller by a system Administrator, to prevent uncontrolled change of format

380.description: When there is an Forecast revision which is saved and approved with a set revision number, the user should be able to create a new estimate from that Forecast (even though several revisions will not evolve to an estimate)
380.acceptanceCriteria: An NH Estimator, with permissions to access a given Project, can export a Project User's forecast BoQ to MS Excel and import this to a NH Estimate to form the basis of a formal NH range estimate.

400.description: Software should have functionality within the estimating/IFT screens to show to the estimator/project user which resource/item/section is driving cost and/or carbon. As an estimator, I want to be able to see what is driving the cost and carbon estimate easily using the same User interface as for estimate production, i.e. not have to leave the estimate production module in order to view this information. For example, PowerBI dashboards or PDF reports are not a replacement for user interface / screens presenting this information in the estimating module itself.
400.acceptanceCriteria:
• A user can open insight reporting data for an estimate directly from within the estimate production software module
• A user can see a report displayed on screen for a cost estimate showing estimated costs and carbon:
   • By Resource in order of value
   • By Item in order of value
   • By Section in order of value

410.description: Flexibility to use either the Item rate derived from the resource buildup or a contractual item rate which may not have a resource level build up.   Software should allow multiple set libraries to be applied or used in producing an estimate. Example on Asset Renewal and M&R use contractor rates which may have or may not have resource buildup or use NH national TPE library or use library from other region or area.Software should allow the item rate buildup to be delinked from resource rate buildup to allow user to enter item rate where resource build in not available. Allow linking with the resource rate build when resource build is available.The above feature should be available in library creation as well as plugin in an item rate or resource build in any estimate.
410.acceptanceCriteria: Multiple libraries of works items can be stored in the system.

420.description: Estimator and project user must be able to see the item and resource quantity by monthly/annually across the estimate schedule when producing the estimate as well as ability to export in excel and report in PDF and Dashboard.
420.acceptanceCriteria:
• A user can generate a report on screen of the estimated total Item quantity profiled over the estimate expenditure duration
• The Item quantity profile shall be available by month for Major Projects, Operation and Maintenance and Renewals estimates
• The Item quantity profile shall be available by year for long term appraisal estimates
• The Item quantity profile report can be exported to MS Excel
• A user can export a total Resource profile by month to MS Excel

430.description:
When producing an estimate; estimator should be able to see comparison of last approved estimate with current estimate within the screens of the estimating module which are used by estimator to produce estimate. Additionally, software should have a Comparator which provides comparison of current or last approved with any historic estimate on scheme.

Software should also show comparison of range (min,ml,max) for estimate from start i.e. estimate 0 to current estimate and when project is delivered Actual cost. The above applies to all estimate types in FR 10
430.acceptanceCriteria:
• A user can generate a comparison report of the estimate in production and the last approved estimate for that scheme, on screen in the software while producing the estimate
• A user can generate a comparison report of any estimate for a scheme vs another estimate for the same scheme, on screen in the software
• A user can generate a report showing the evolution of the estimated cost for a scheme, by selecting the approved estimates to include in the report. The report will display:
   • The estimates in chronological order
   • The estimate ID and date
   • The estimate classification
   • The estimated total minimum, most-likely, and maximum cost
• The report shall be able to include the ‘Final Cost’ where this has been uploaded for a completed scheme

470.description: Whole life Carbon calculated in software in accordance with PAS2080 with necessary sub modules as discussed and provided by Circular Ecology.
470.acceptanceCriteria: The CCET carbon libraries hold data at the granularity of PAS 2080 modules / sub-modules set out in reference document "W.16 - Modules for Whole Life Carbon and alignment to latest RICS guidance.xls" provided by Circular Ecology

490.description: For each client baseline cost estimate, the user should be able to view an identical client carbon estimate
490.acceptanceCriteria: The CCET generates a carbon estimate for a cost estimate in the system by automatically applying carbon Item and Resource libraries (including cost-to-carbon factors) to the unchanged Segments, Sections and Items in the cost estimate, i.e. the basis of the cost and carbon estimates is identical from Item level upwards.

500.description: Software should allow library / user input of negative carbon factors in the modules suggested by Circular Ecology, e.g. landscaping, lands, 3rd Party income, Module D(if being delivered in scope)
500.acceptanceCriteria: The carbon libraries can hold negative carbon emission factors for each module and sub-module.

511.description: Software should flag a carbon factor which has not been assured by an assurer(different from project user).
511.acceptanceCriteria: Carbon factors used in an estimate that have not been assured by National Highways are identified in the CCET by an 'Unassured' flag for the relevant Resource.

520.description: Enable results from a controlled asphalt calculator to be used in the software to produce carbon emission factors for specific design mixes to satisfy quality requirements (using existing ASPECT model and similar build to existing concrete calculator on Circular Ecology web-enabled system).
520.acceptanceCriteria:
• As an estimator I can download the latest version of the calculator from the landing page.
• As an estimator I can open the calculator and launch the Excel Add-in to connect to CCET.
• As an estimator I can change values in the calculator and with one-click get the Cost and Carbon values for the calculated BOQ Item/Resource quantities.

530.description: Identify resources where carbon has been manually entered by the user
530.acceptanceCriteria: The CCET identifies whether a Resource in an estimate is linked to a library or delinked.

540.description: Enable results from a controlled concrete calculator to be used in the software to produce carbon emission factors for specific design mixes to satisfy quality requirements (using similar build to existing concrete calculator on Circular Ecology web-enabled system).
540.acceptanceCriteria:
• As an estimator I can import the BOQ from the calculator into CCET via the Excel Add-in.
• As an estimator I can also upload the calculator as a document to the estimate.
• As an estimator or model administrator I can configure any model which produces a BOQ with Items and Quantities to work with the Excel Add-in.

550.description: Enable results from a steel calculator to be used in the software to produce carbon emission factors for specific design mixes to satisfy quality requirements (using similar build to existing concrete calculator on Circular Ecology web-enabled system).
550.acceptanceCriteria: • As a calculator/model administrator I can output just Items or Items with alternative Resource build-ups in the BOQ to support resource variations for multiple mix variations.

560.description: Record C2, C3 and C4 emission factors at the Resource level, and generate calculations for all estimates as per Scope Table A.
560.acceptanceCriteria: The Carbon libraries contain fields for each of modules C2, C3 and C4 at Resource level.

570.description: As an estimator I want to view the Carbon risk, opportunity and uncertainty allowances at Project, Programme and Portfolio Risk in embedded screens within the software for estimate types as per Scope Table A.
570.acceptanceCriteria: An Estimator can view the following Carbon Risk Allowances side by side with the base estimate amounts on embedded screens within the estimate production interface for all Estimates:

590.description: Outturn profile of Embodied carbon to be calculated for the assumed carbon quantities from each time period and the carbon emission factors in respective time period
590.acceptanceCriteria: CCET calculates carbon profile using the resource quantities required for each time period multiplied by the associated carbon factors and provides KgCo2e for each respective PAS2080 module.

601.description:
Ability to overwrite the calculated top-down carbon risk allowance. Where there is no risk register with quantified carbon, software should have the functionality to insert a top down risk allowance for carbon at cost element level.

When producing an authority estimate (baseline), where there is no risk register software should carry out automatic cost to carbon risk calculations based on risk% age or risk allowance in risk register at cost element level with proportionate allocation across PAS 2080 modules as previous discussed and details provided to Benchmark.

This applies to all carbon estimate types as per Table A in the Scope.
601.acceptanceCriteria:
• A User can apply a cost risk/uncertainty allowance at Section level within the OMR cost estimate, based on either a risk register or a top-down risk approach

• The software shall apply cost to carbon risk calculations based on risk allowance in risk register at Section level with proportionate allocation to the relevant PAS 2080 modules (B2—B5 for O&M estimates)

• A User shall be able to edit the cost and carbon risk allowances generated by the default top-down approach

610.description: Software should include a Benchmark template for each estimate type as per FR 10 and allow benchmark figures to be inserted into the template to allow the comparison to be made and reported for each estimate output. Nb. CERT/CESS/RET already includes this.
610.acceptanceCriteria:
• An administrator has the ability to enter a configure custom metric or benchmark ‘yardstick’ for an estimate type, specifying:
   • The benchmark metric name
   • The benchmark metric unit
• An Administrator is able to enter benchmark values for each metric or ‘yardstick’ in a controlled table for an estimate type
• A user is able to enter a value in an estimate-specific field for the benchmark metric name and unit and the estimated cost value to be divided by the metric
• A user can generate a report on screen showing the estimate-specific values populated for the benchmark metrics, and the corresponding benchmark metric values maintained in the administrator-controlled table for that estimate type
• The report can be exported to PDF and Excel format
• The report states the price base of the values
• The report states the project name, estimate name and estimate ID

640.description: Produce an estimate using outturn estimate costs , that does not have a single base date across all elements and some cost elements, or all cost elements might be at outturn prices inclusive of all inflation
640.acceptanceCriteria: Each Estimate in the CCET has a base date (the common price base of the estimate before application of inflation)

670.description: Ability to overwrite the calculated top-down carbon risk allowance. Where there is no risk register with quantified carbon, software should have the functionality to insert a top down risk allowance for carbon at cost element level.
670.acceptanceCriteria: An Estimator can enter Cost and Carbon Risk top-down to a Section in an Estimate, instead of importing a risk register, e.g. if no risk register is available.

680.description: As a user, I want the ability to plug carbon factor at an item rate level manually, which is delinked from the resource build-up for that item.
680.acceptanceCriteria: An Estimator can "delink" the resources in an Item from the Resource Library, so that the Resource Rate is not updated by any change in the library value and can be edited by the Estimator.

690.description: View the carbon expenditure profile over time by WBS (Work Breakdown Structure) and by Resource in embedded screens within the estimate
690.acceptanceCriteria: • A user can generate a report on screen within the estimating module displays estimated carbon over time periods, e.g. Financial Year, by WBS

700.description: For an Item/Resource, if the carbon data is not found in the carbon library then use the cost to carbon factor to  generate the impacts for all PAS2080 modules.  Software should allow this to be done in two ways - 1) allow cost to carbon factors to be included in library(baseline/project specific) for auto allocation 2) Allow plugged in resource or item level cost to carbon factors to be plugged in the estimate.
700.acceptanceCriteria: The CCET holds cost-to-carbon factors in carbon data libraries at Resource level with an assigned Resource Group.

710.description: Record C1 at the project level using a placeholder and a configurable calculation to generate C2
710.acceptanceCriteria: An Estimator can manually enter the estimated total carbon impact for PAS 2080 Module C1 for the whole project.

720.description: Record C1 emission factors at the Resource level, and generate calculations
720.acceptanceCriteria: Carbon Libraries for New Construction lifecycle Stage (PAS 2080 Before Use) can store data for module C1, as well as the PAS 2080 Stage A modules.

730.description: When producing a Capex PAS2080 stage A, the library will need to populate the Stage C2-C4 emission factors
730.acceptanceCriteria: Carbon Libraries for New Construction lifecycle Stage (PAS 2080 Before Use) store data for modules C2, C3, C4 as well as the PAS 2080 Stage A modules.

739.description:
As an Estimator I need to be able to produce Routine Maintenance cost estimates for two purposes:

1) Impact of a CAPEX scheme (MP delivered) on Routine Maintenance over a user-defined assessment period of up to 200 years.

2) Detailed forecast spend on Routine Maintenance activities for a specific National Highways SRN Area (e.g. Area 10, SW, EMAD etc.)
739.acceptanceCriteria:
See SRS Chapter 3&4 for Standalone Detailed O&M estimate for Acceptance Criteria and Design Specifications for (up to 20 years) assessment period.

• A CCET User can produce an OMR estimate for the Without and With Scheme scenarios to produce the impact on cost and carbon of a CAPEX* scheme on OMR duties over a user-configurable estimate duration from 1 to 200 years.

• *CAPEX work can be either an enhancement or renewal scheme, delivered and funded by National Highways Major Projects (RIP, CIP etc.) or Operations (Area 10, Area SW etc.)

• A CCET User can view and amend the OMR estimate data at an annual level of detail over the assessment period

740.description:
As an Estimator, I need to be able to calculate the Intervention Quantity for each Routine Maintenance activity, based on the Quantity of Asset x Intervention Frequency.

Quantity of Asset will be based upon each Areas Network Information or Estimator specified quantity.

 Intervention Frequency will default to the ADAMR Baseline Frequency, or the Estimator can specify an ILM Intervention Frequency. The Intervention Frequencies can be set annually (i.e. different frequencies for each year of the assessment period)
740.acceptanceCriteria:
For an O&M estimate, there is:
    • an editable field for each Item of work that contains the quantity of asset to which that Operation / Maintenance Item is carried out.
    • an editable field for each Item of work that contains the annual intervention frequency at which that Operation / Maintenance Item is carried out.
    • a calculated field containing the annual intervention quantity for each Item, i.e. the annual quantity of times that the O&M Item is carried out in a year
• The CCET produces the Annual Intervention Quantities for each O&M Item through the following calculation: Asset Quantity x Annual Intervention Frequency
• The O&M Item library contains a field for Default Annual Intervention Frequency for each Item, that can be populated with the default frequency, e.g. the ADAMR Baseline Frequency
• An Estimator can directly enter and edit the asset quantities into the O&M estimate
  • or upload the asset quantities from Excel
• An Estimator can directly enter and edit annual intervention frequencies for each Item within the estimate, e.g. to provide alternative intervention frequencies from the default
   • or upload the intervention frequencies for each Item from Excel
• An Estimator can directly edit the total calculated intervention quantities for an Item for each year in the assessment period.
   • or upload the intervention quantities from Excel

750.description: As an Estimator I need to be able to apply the latest contractual Routine Maintenance activity unit rate for the relevant Area. This unit rate library will be stored for each Area and updated on an annual basis.
750.acceptanceCriteria: The CCET can hold Item rate libraries for Operation and Maintenance lifecycle works.

751.description:
As an Estimator I need a "generic - NH level" first principles resource build-up for each Routine Maintenance activity unit rate, which is decoupled from the contractual Routine Maintenance activity unit rate. This "generic" resource build-up will be used for carbon and resource forecasting.

The software will have the capability to replace these "generic" unit build-ups with Area specific build-ups over time and link to the Item unit rate.
751.acceptanceCriteria: Multiple libraries of works items can be stored in the system.

760.description:
As an Estimator, I need to be able to produce a detailed 12-60 month Routine Maintenance cost forecast. 

I need to be able to input actual Routine Maintenance intervention quantities, on a monthly basis, and then revise the original forecast Routine Maintenance activity quantities for the subsequent assessment period (i.e. rolling 12-month forecast). These revisions will be user input data, not autogenerated by the software.
760.acceptanceCriteria:
• An Estimator can create a detailed O&M estimate for up to 20-year assessment period at a monthly level of detail
• An Estimator can apply to each O&M activity / item a default monthly activity profile over January- December (i.e. the percentage of annual intervention quantities to be delivered in each month)
• An Estimator can edit the intervention / item quantities to be delivered in each month from the default profile’s values for each O&M activity
• There is an administrator-controlled library of O&M expenditure profiles that are applied to an O&M activity / Item to profile quantities by month (January-December)

See SRS Chapter 6 for Project User forecasting vs. baseline

780.description:
I need the software to collate the forecast Routine Maintenance costs to the National Highways O&M WBS, which currently aligns with the M&R contract structure for use in the detailed Routine Maintenance spend forecast (i.e. Schedule A, C, D etc.) over the assessment period.

The estimated cost data within the WBS can then be re-organised to produce the impact of a CAPEX project (MP or Operations delivered) on Routine Maintenance over the assessment period, to satisfy the requirements of the BCR process.

 This will include the application of inflation, discounting and Market Adjustment Factors. This will require the software to produce multiple outputs each for specific purposes (e.g. real terms, nominal terms, post-discounting etc.)

Please note FR780 is also covered in chapter 2 – Long Term Appraisals.
780.acceptanceCriteria:
The CCET has an administrator-controlled Estimate Type library, that contains a configurable template for an O&M estimate (unpriced) and can be configured by NH to align with a standard WBS for an O&M.
• When an O&M estimate is initiated, the Estimate Type library populates the Estimate Shell with the template structure configured in the Estimate Type library.
   • See SRS Chapter 9, Estimate Workflows, Lifecycle Estimate (Output) Type Configurable Library.
• The CCET stores libraries of O&M Items/activities with configurable Items/activity codes, descriptions and units, so that cost estimates using the O&M Item/activity Library collate costs aligned with the NH O&M WBS.

• An Estimator can produce estimates of the impact of a Capex project on O&M costs by entering the Capex project asset quantities to the O&M estimate and applying Item/activity libraries to generate the estimated cost of the Capex project’s impact.
• An Estimator can produce an O&M estimate for an identified ‘Without Scheme’ scenario and an O&M estimate for an identified ‘With Scheme’ scenario in consistent format
• An Estimator can generate a report of the difference between estimates for a ‘Without Scheme’ scenario and ‘With Scheme’ scenario and see the estimated incremental impact
The CCET can apply the following to estimated costs in real terms (at the set price base of the estimate):
  • Inflation factors per month to produce costs in nominal terms inclusive of inflation allowances (factors generated from a configurable library of inflation indices)
  • GDP deflator factors to deflate costs for net present cost calculations (generated from a configurable library of inflation / deflation indices)
  • Discount factors for economic assessment (generated from a configurable library of discount rates)
  • Market adjustment factors for economic assessment (generated from a configurable library of market adjustment factors)
  • The cost impact of the each of the above factors shall be clearly identified in estimate outputs

Please note FR780 is also covered in chapter 2 – Long Term Appraisals.

781.description:
As an Estimator, I want to be able to associate items of work (and their underlying resources and the costs and carbon impact) with an asset class so that I can report the capex and Opex and renewals works (individually and combined) by asset class.

Similarly, I want to be able to associate items of work (and underlying resources / costs / carbon) with alternative breakdown structures' coding so that I can report the estimate by these breakdown structures, e.g. ICMS, CESMM
781.acceptanceCriteria: The CCET Item libraries (for all lifecycle stages) include a field to hold the default asset for that Item of works

782.description: As an estimator, I want to be able to segment the Opex estimate (and MP and Renewals and therefore WLC estimate) so that I can see the quantity, cost and carbon per segment (capex, Opex, renewals, WLC)
782.acceptanceCriteria: As a user I can segment estimates (for each of the FR10 outputs types) buildup and then report cost and carbon for the created segments.

790.description: Record yearly intervention frequencies for each Item (activity) undertaken to maintain an Asset - Covered by FR 1840
790.acceptanceCriteria: The Item libraries in the CCET for O&M works have a field to store the default annual intervention frequency for that Item (O&M activity).

800.description: Risk - Allow the user to directly input Risk at a section level (Top down) - See FR 1790
800.acceptanceCriteria:
An NH Estimator can input risk allowances for an O&M estimate for each Section of the estimate over which risk allowances that is designated as a level at which risk allowances are to be allocated.

An NH Estimator can input risk allowances for the following:
▪Project cost risk / opportunity and uncertainty
▪Project carbon risk / opportunity and uncertainty (see FR1080, FR1090 and FR1100)
▪Programme / Portfolio cost risk / opportunity and uncertainty
▪Programme / Portfolio carbon risk / opportunity and uncertainty (see FR1080, FR1090 and FR1100)

810.description: Risk (long term goal) -Allow the user to import a risk register into the application for M&R to apply at a section level. - See FR 1790
810.acceptanceCriteria:
The CCET shall enable a project risk register to be imported to an O&M cost estimate and generate the risk / opportunity / uncertainty allowances at a Section level.

Note: the process for calculation and allocation of cost risk / opportunity and uncertainty allowances for O&M estimates, the granularity of allocation across cost elements and by employer / supplier is to be confirmed by NH – see RFIs ref. B.16 and B.17

820.description:
As an estimator, I need to produce an estimate for M&R in accordance with the NH WBS for Routine Operation and Maintenance, covering:dedicated Cost Elements for O&M - the library would require to store the WBS for the M&R estimate to cover the below.
- Cyclical Duties
- Non - Cyclical Duties 
- Cost Reimbursable Services
820.acceptanceCriteria: The CCET holds a configurable 'Estimate Output Type' library that contains the following data for each Estimate Type:

830.description:
Dedicated Cost Elements for O&M - the library would require to store the WBS for the M&R estimate to cover the below.
- Cyclical Duties
- Non - Cyclical Duties 
- Cost Reimbursable Services 
- Task Orders  

See FR 820
830.acceptanceCriteria: The CCET holds a configurable 'Estimate Output Type' library that contains the following data for each Estimate Type:

840.description: As an Estimator, I need to be able to reference the Routine Maintenance cost estimate to the agreed data hierarchy structure (e.g. Portfolio - Ops, Region - NW, Area - Area 10, EIN etc.) This data hierarchy will allow the Estimator to search the estimate database for the relevant output and link to associated CAPEX outputs. The data hierarchy is to be confirmed with NH but may include: OD Portfolio - Programme - M&R/Asset Renewals and identifiers for Region, Route, Segment, Asset Classes to cost elements to activity/items to resources level coding. This coding needs to be based on a connected NH WBS, CBS, ActBS and AssBS.
840.acceptanceCriteria:
• An O&M estimate is assigned to the following administrator-configurable setup:
• A project or scheme (which can be a defined O&M Contract or scope)
• A Programme
• A Portfolio
• An Area and Region
• A configurable location reference, such as ‘Route’
• For a Whole life Cost and carbon estimate A ‘Parent’ full lifecycle costing estimate and associated capex estimate
• An Estimator can assign an Asset to each Item/activity in a O&M cost estimate
• CCET will have functionality to connected NH WBS, CBS, ActBS and AssBS to produce whole life cost and carbon estimates.
• The O&M estimated costs can be reported by Asset
• Assets are assigned to Items/activities from an administrator-controlled configurable library of Assets that is standardised across lifecycle stages
• The standardised Assets assigned to capex Items, Operation and Maintenance Items (activities) and Asset Renewals Items connect Items across lifecycle stages
• A CCET user can browse estimates within the agreed NH Enterprise, following the data hierarchy and open the estimates directly from the browser interface.
• A CCET user can search estimates using NH-agreed data structure codes such as estimate ID, estimate title, project names, Region, Area, Programme, Portfolio, etc.

850.description: Develop hierarchy in the application - Section (e.g. Lump Sum Duties - Schedule A) > Series / Cost Element (e.g. 400 - Road Restraints) > Asset Type (e.g. Arrester beds) > Item > Resource See FR 820-840
850.acceptanceCriteria:
The O&M Item libraries stored in the CCET can contain configurable resource-build-ups for Items / Activities and codes assigning the Item to default Sections and Asset.

The CCET contains libraries of the O&M Resources used to populate O&M works’ Items / activities

Please refer to SRS Chapter 11, Data Libraries for details of the library of Estimate Output Types containing configurable estimate templates to populate the estimate shell for O&M estimates.

860.description:
As an Estimator I need the software to be able to produce a TPE Routine Maintenance output at Cost Element level.

Probabilistic estimating / TPE for Long-Term Appraisal cost estimated is not included in the CCET Phase 3 functional requirements. We propose to apply the Acceptance Criteria for FR860 and FR1260 and Feature Design for these functional requirements to NH Long-Term Appraisal cost estimates to provide this coverage.

Please see the following related Functional Requirements:
▪ FR140 (SS Chapter 6, Supplier Forecasting) refers to converting a supplier forecast to a NH range estimate. (This is produced through existing CCET Phase 1 functionality for Major Projects, FR860 for Routine O&M and FR1260 for Asset Renewals.)
▪FR430 (SRS Chapter 8, Reporting) refers to comparison reports of the current estimate vs. the last approved estimate / other previous estimates for a project to include showing the range of an estimate where this is in place
▪ CCET Phase 1 FR30 (Delivered)
▪ CCET Phase 1 FR10 (Delivered)
▪ CCET Phase 1 FR21 (Partially Delivered – remaining items are PDF and CDF charts covered in FR860 and FR1260 acceptance criteria)
▪CCET Phase 2 FRs bullet point 6, “Configure and upload a ‘baseline’ carbon resource library… in three-point estimating format….. – addressed by SRS Chapter 11, Data Libraries, FR410, Acceptance Criterion 8 inter alia.
860.acceptanceCriteria:
The CCET produces a probabilistic estimate of an Operation and Maintenance cost estimate as well as a single-point deterministic cost estimate. The probabilistic cost estimate is produced using Monte Carlo simulation of input three-point estimates for the total cost of the following: 
- Each cost element in the estimate build-up in real terms prior to inflation 
- The estimated delivery schedule for the project / contract, i.e. the estimated start and finish dates of the cost element's scope (there will no range for an O&M estimate of annual cost) 
- The estimated inflation forecast

870.description:
As an Estimator, I need the software to apply forecast inflation from the unit rate base date (PAFI adjusted annually) over the assessment period based on the approved NH inflation series.

I also need the software to apply inflation, discounting and Market Adjustment Factors, for long term OPEX cost assessments.
870.acceptanceCriteria:
• An Estimator can set a common price base date for an O&M estimate by item/activity.
• The price base of the O&M estimate is clearly stated in the estimate production screens and estimate reports / outputs
• The CCET stores a library of approved inflation indices in an administrator-controlled library
• The inflation indices are stored as monthly index values
• The CCET applies inflation profile calculated using the relevant inflation index series selected from the library by an estimator to calculate an inflation allowance from the common estimate price base date to the time of expenditure of costs across the assessment period
• The CCET applies inflation profile calculated using the inflation index to the estimated monthly O&M costs
• The CCET inflation functionality produce outturn costs over the assessment period and summarise to show at monthly and yearly level. (max 20 years)
Please also refer to SRS Chapter 2, Long-term appraisal.

880.description:
As an Estimator, for detailed Routine Maintenance cost estimates (1), I need the software to apply a spend profile for each Routine Maintenance activity on a monthly basis (i.e. grass cutting only applied between April and October). 

For long term CAPEX linked Routine Maintenance estimates (2) I need the spend profile to be applied at an annual level of detail.
880.acceptanceCriteria: The CCET has an administrator-controlled library of default expenditure profiles for O&M estimates

890.description: Inflation - Apply monthly inflation indices to Item rates in base estimate to generate inflated estimates for each year across the assessment period (where assessment period is 5 years or less) - then summarise at a yearly level (for longer assessment periods)See FR 870
890.acceptanceCriteria: The CCET has an administrator-controlled library of default inflation indices

900.description: As an Estimator, I want an easy way of setting an intervention quantity (i.e. scope) for each year of a long term assessment period. Long-term projections for intervention quantities for M&R estimates - Calculate intervention quantities for a reference year (e.g. detailed year 1 or average over first 5 years) and project to apply across the assessment period.
900.acceptanceCriteria:
• The O&M Item library contains a field for Default Annual Intervention Frequency for each Item, that can be populated with the default frequency, e.g. the ADAMR Baseline Frequency
• The library Item, including default intervention frequency, can be automatically allocated to an Item in an O&M estimate by matching Item code or Item description
• The Estimator can bulk upload asset quantities from Excel for each Item in an O&M estimate
• The Estimator can bulk upload annual intervention frequencies from Excel for each Item in an O&M estimate, so the CCET generates total intervention quantities for a given year of the assessment period.
• The Estimator can select a reference year and copy that year’s calculated annual intervention quantities over the remaining years of an assessment period up to 20 years

910.description: As per 7.14, the software should be able to produce multiple outputs from a data Dashboard to display the cost estimate in a format required by NH (e.g. real terms, nominal terms, assessment period, level of detail - monthly/annual etc.)
910.acceptanceCriteria:
• A user can view a dashboard of an Operations and Maintenance cost estimate displaying multiple data for the estimate, including:
   • The estimate in real terms excluding inflation
   • The estimate in nominal terms including inflation
   • The period covered by the estimate
   • Costs by month and by year

920.description: See FR 910 - View the Estimate in Real Terms without Inflation

930.description: See FR 910 - View the estimated costs in real terms at a set price based, inclusive of relative price growth.

940.description:
As an Estimator I need the software to apply carbon costs (CO2e) to the estimate Routine Maintenance activities. The carbon costs will be derived from the Routine Maintenance activity resource build-ups.

The software should have the capability to apply a carbon inflation/deflation factor to the baseline Routine Maintenance carbon costs which could be applied, following review and approval from NH. The inflation / deflation profiles should be stored and maintained in a dedicated library.
940.acceptanceCriteria:
The CCET calculates carbon equivalent value (CO2e) at Resource level to PAS 2080 modules / sub-modules recommended in reference document "W.16 - Modules for Whole Life Carbon and alignment to latest RICS guidance.xls" provided by Circular Ecology.

Background carbon decarbonisation profile(s) can be stored in an administrator-controlled library within the CCET

The expected yearly rate of general background carbon decarbonisation is stored as percentages and the CCET calculates deflation coefficients for each year from an estimate baseline date

The CCET shows decarbonisation coefficients below total carbon base estimate + carbon risk allowances for each month / year shown in an estimate output.

The CCET shows the carbon deflation amount and impact separately within an estimate output.

The CCET calculates carbon equivalent values for each PAS 2080 modules / sub-modules recommended in reference document "W.16 - Modules for Whole Life Carbon and alignment to latest RICS guidance.xls" provided by Circular Ecology, including the sequestered carbon modules recommended in this file.

950.description:
As an Estimator, I need, B6/B7 to be estimated in the Routine Maintenance element of the software, for each year.
This could be estimated at the Area level or asset level.
950.acceptanceCriteria:
• An Item/activity can be created for each one of modules B1, B6, B7, B8 and B9 at the Estimate-level to hold carbon impacts with data organised by month for the entire estimate (e.g. a whole Area)

• Individual Item/activity can be created for each one of modules B1, B6, B7, B8 and B9 at a Section-level to hold carbon impacts with data organised by month at Asset level

• Modules B1, B6, B7, B8 and B9 carbon impacts can be uploaded by month

• The CCET system can record and estimate B6 and B7 at the item/activity or resource level by month, organised into separate sections for B6 and B7.

• CCET reports can aggregate monthly values to report yearly carbon values for modules B1, B6, B7, B8 and B9 for B8.

960.description: As an Estimator, I want to be able to record sequestered carbon within the estimate calculated in accordance with RICS 2nd Edition of WL Carbon Assessment as per the module structure provided by Circular Ecology - this may be a placeholder at estimate level.

970.description:
There may be multiple Routine Maintenance cost estimates for any project (i.e. multiple options). The Estimator should be able to select a preferred carbon estimate for any project

For detailed Routine Maintenance cost estimates (1), the software will have the capability to update the estimate on a monthly basis, with actual interventions delivered and impact on carbon costs.

For Routine Maintenance estimates associated with a CAPEX cost estimate (2), the Estimator can update any previous Routine Maintenance cost estimate to reflect the changes in the CAPEX cost estimate
970.acceptanceCriteria:
• Multiple O&M estimates, each with a unique estimate ID, can be produced for a project.
• An Estimator can select any estimate for a project and designate that estimate as the ‘Preferred Carbon Estimate’.
• There can be only one designated ‘Preferred Carbon Estimate’ for a project at any one time.

Please refer to SRS Chapter 6, Project User Forecasting functionality for updates with actual / reforecast interventions

• For a completed O&M estimate, An Estimator can duplicate the O&M estimate, assign a new

980.description: See FR 950 - An efficient way of uploading B6/B7 data for each year in the assessment period.

990.description: As an Estimator I need the software to be capable of capturing carbon costs monthly for up to the first 5-years. I should be able to define the period I require monthly carbon cost forecasting. For the remaining assessment period, carbon should be captured at an annual level
990.acceptanceCriteria:
The CCET shall produce O&M estimates at a monthly level of detail and show the carbon equivalent value per month of the estimate’s assessment period.
The CCET shall be able to report carbon equivalent value for O&M estimates for each year of the estimate’s assessment period.
An Estimator can specify the assessment period of a detailed O&M estimate to cover a maximum period of 20 years.

1000.description: The software should be configured to the PAS2080 requirements to align with the RICS 2nd edition as per recommendation of modules provided by Circular Ecology.
1000.acceptanceCriteria: The CCET carbon libraries hold data at the granularity of PAS 2080 modules / sub-modules set out in reference document "W.16 - Modules for Whole Life Carbon and alignment to latest RICS guidance.xls" provided by Circular Ecology

1010.description: Enter B8 user carbon at a project level for each year within the project (possibly by month).

1020.description: As an Estimator, the software should have the future capability (I.e. placeholder) to include B1 (Asset in Use) carbon costs within the carbon estimate. This should be a placeholder only, not the full working solution at this stage of development

1030.description: As an Estimator I need the software to have the capability to tag all activities within the estimate as either B2 or B3, for reporting purposes as per PAS 2080 requirements.
1030.acceptanceCriteria: The O&M Item library contains a field for each Operation and Maintenance Item ("activity") that stores a default PAS 2080 module for the Item.

1040.description: See FR 1020 - The system requires the ability to record B1 across a time series.

1050.description: See FR 950 - Ability to estimate B6/B7 at an item and resource level, across a time series

1060.description: Produce a detailed estimate for B2-B5 that captures data at sub module level, e.g. transportation of deconstructed materials, transport of new materials, construction and installation, wastage. They will require granular analysis of contributing factors.
1060.acceptanceCriteria: The CCET carbon libraries hold data at the granularity of PAS 2080 modules / sub-modules set out in reference document "W.16 - Modules for Whole Life Carbon and alignment to latest RICS guidance.xls" provided by Circular Ecology

1070.description: The system should be able to store Cost to Carbon factors at a base date and apply these factors to resources in an estimate in order to plug gaps - i.e. resources with no carbon emission factor in the library
1070.acceptanceCriteria: The CCET stores cost-to-carbon factors in an administrator-controlled library or libraries for application to each lifecycle costing stage.

1080.description: See FR 670 - Ability to overwrite the calculated top-down carbon risk allowance
1080.acceptanceCriteria:
The CCET will automatically calculate a top-down carbon risk / opportunity / uncertainty allowance at Section/Cost element level, by applying the base estimate carbon/cost intensity to the cost risk / opportunity / uncertainty allowance for that Section/Cost Element. The CCET will automatically calculate top-down carbon risk / opportunity / uncertainty allowances for Project level risk and Programme / Portfolio Risk.

The software shall apply these cost to carbon risk calculations based on the risk / opportunity / uncertainty allowance at Section/Cost Element level with proportionate allocation to the relevant PAS 2080 modules (B2-B3 for O&M estimates).

A User shall be able to edit and overwrite the carbon risk / opportunity / uncertainty allowances generated by the default top-down approach.

1090.description: See FR 670 - Calculate Carbon Risk and Uncertainty Allowance at the Cost Header (Cost Element) level using the Cost to Carbon Intensity Factor

1100.description: As an estimator, I want to include risk / opportunity / uncertainty allowances at Project, Programme, and Portfolio level

1120.description: As an Estimator I need the software to produce detailed reports based on user queries for both cost and carbon. This will include cost/carbon spend over time and by WBS or Resource. The reports will also be able to compare cost/carbon forecasts against the baseline cost estimate(s) and across Programme and Portfolio level
1120.acceptanceCriteria:
• A user can select what data he/she wants to see in a report via some dynamic fields, which act as user queries, including:
   • The WBS level of the report
   • The period covered by the report
• A user can generate a report comparing a submitted cost or carbon forecast vs. a reference baseline cost or carbon estimate for a scheme
• A user can generate a report comparing selected submitted cost or carbon forecasts comprising a programme vs. a reference baseline cost or carbon estimate for the programme
• A user can generate a report comparing selected submitted cost or carbon forecasts comprising a portfolio vs. a reference baseline cost or carbon estimate for that portfolio

1130.description: See 1120 - View a table with Spend Profile calculations for Item Qty (Asset Qty * Intervention Frequency) and carbon expenditure over the assessment period. This would be monthly for the first 5 years, and yearly thereafter for longer term.
1130.acceptanceCriteria:
An Estimator can select what data he/she wants to see in a report via some dynamic fields, which act as user queries, including:
     • The WBS level of the report
     • The period covered by the report
• The CCET produces a carbon expenditure profile table for an estimate showing the carbon equivalent value per month of the estimate assessment period.
• The CCET produces a table for an estimate showing the Item Quantity per month of the estimate assessment period.
• An Estimator can generate a report comparing a submitted cost or carbon forecast vs. a reference baseline cost or carbon estimate for a project
• An Estimator can generate a report comparing selected submitted cost or carbon forecasts comprising a programme vs. a reference baseline cost or carbon estimate for the programme
• An Estimator can generate a report comparing selected submitted cost or carbon forecasts comprising a portfolio vs. a reference baseline cost or carbon estimate for that portfolio

1140.description: See 1120 - View the carbon expenditure profile over time by WBS (Work Breakdown Structure) and by Resource
1140.acceptanceCriteria:
• A user can generate a report of carbon expenditure over time by WBS and by resources
• The user can select the WBS level of the report so that carbon expenditure is shown in a logical format

1150.description: See FR350 - Compare Estimated Carbon Impact with Carbon Reduction Targets at Scheme, Programme and Portfolio levels
1150.acceptanceCriteria:
• An authorised user can enter a Carbon Reduction Target (CAP) for a project in the software
• A user can see a report or dashboard that compares the Carbon Reduction Target(CAP) with an estimate for the project
• I should also be able to see a reports showing the aggregated latest estimate data versus the aggregated carbon reduction targets at Programme or Portfolio Level
• The data is based on approved estimates only and informed by either the preferred estimates or reference estimates
• As a user I can see how a forecast submitted by a Project User compares to the Carbon Reduction Target (CAP) for that project

1153.description:
As an Estimator I need to be able to produce Asset Renewal cost estimates for two purposes:

1) Impact of a CAPEX scheme (MP or Operations delivered) on Asset Renewals over a user defined assessment period of up to 120 years.

2) Detailed standalone Asset Renewal cost estimate for a single scheme
1153.acceptanceCriteria:
As an estimator I can produce an estimate for periodic asset renewals within a long-term appraisal of a capex estimate in addition to a standalone estimate for an asset renewal project.

Please see SRS Chapter 2 for the specification of Long-Term Appraisal estimates.

1160.description:
For standalone detailed Asset Renewal cost estimates (2), as an Estimator I need the software to receive an unpriced Schedule of Items from Excel (or 2D / 3D take-off feature) and apply the relevant contractual item rate (SDF or other) to price the proposed scope of work, refer to 9.13 for further details

The unpriced Schedule of Items must be produced following the NH Ops WBS and can produced either by:
1) NH Direct and Indirect (including TTM) parametric models
2) Estimator/Supplier produced Schedule of Items from quantity take-off
1160.acceptanceCriteria: • As an estimator, I can import and update a schedule of Assets / Items and quantities into an estimate.

1161.description:
For assessment of Asset Renewal costs associated with the CAPEX scheme (1), as an Estimator I need the software to apply relevant renewal unit rates to the asset quantities input by the Estimator within the long term OPEX assessment .  In addition to these unit rates, there will be a top down inclusion for Prelims, TTM, Design, SU and Other costs.

For assessment of Asset Renewal costs associated with the CAPEX scheme, as an Estimator I need to be able to tag Asset Renewal quantities and associated activities as either New, Remove or Renewed within the software

The all-in composite rates shall be stored and maintained in a dedicated library.
1161.acceptanceCriteria: The Items within the CCET Item libraries are configurable by an administrator.  The administrator can store Item rates in the library that are composite rates (for example including allowances for indirect costs such as traffic management, utilities or other costs).

1170.description: "As an Estimator I need to be able to reference the Routine Maintenance cost estimate to the agreed data hierarchy structure (e.g. Portfolio - Ops, Region - NW, Area - Area 10, Route - M6, EIN, Do Something or Do Nothing scenario etc.)This data hierarchy will allow the Estimator to search the estimate database for the relevant output and link to associated OPEX outputs"

1180.description: For standalone detailed Asset Renewal cost estimates, as an Estimator I need the software to capture and display estimated costs to a admin-configurable cost element structure, as per the National Highways Asset Renewals CESS, which is reflective of the 3D Process
1180.acceptanceCriteria: • As an administrator I can create configurable cost elements and sections in an estimating template similar to NH Asset Renewal CESS aligned with 3D framework. This template will be configurable and controlled by an administrator.

1190.description:
For standalone detailed Asset Renewal cost estimates, as an Estimator  I need to be able to specify the source of the unit rate to reflect the scheme specific commercial variables and for the software to select and apply the relevant Supplier rate, based on the Estimator selected variables.

Currently this includes: selection of Region, selection of Supplier Lot, selection of  Supplier sub-lot, selection of specific Supplier and selection of scheme specific delivery details (e.g. season, time, day)

I need the ability to select any of the above scheme specific commercial variables as Unknown, and the software to select a Supplier unit rate to apply with the cost estimate. This process of supplier selection could be based on the current SDF pricing templates.
1190.acceptanceCriteria: The CCET can store supplier-specific Item and Resource libraries that an estimator can select to apply to an estimate.  An estimator can select the supplier-specific library to apply to the Items in an estimate.

1191.description:
As an Estimator I need a "generic - NH level" first principles resource build-up for each Asset Renewal Item unit rate, which is decoupled from the contractual Asset Renewal Item unit rate.  Carbon calculations (and resource demand reports) may need to use the generic resource build-up; whereas cost estimates may need to use just the contractual unit rate. 

I need the capability for the "generic - NH level" resource build-ups to be superseded over time to be replaced with  Supplier specific  first principle resource build-ups for each Asset Renewal Item unit rate.
1191.acceptanceCriteria: Multiple libraries of works items can be stored in the system.

1192.description:
As an Estimator I need to be able to produce a new first principal resource level build-up for an activity not included within the NH Asset Renewal Item library. The software should allow the user to build the new item using the NH Asset Renewal resource library. Each new Item should be able to be assigned to a specific Supplier engaged within the cost estimate.

Following a separate NH review/approval process the software  should allow the update of the Item library with approved "Star rates" for use in other Asset Renewal estimates
1192.acceptanceCriteria: An Estimator can create an Item in an estimate using Resources from the relevant Resource library for that estimate and Item.

1193.description: For assessment of Asset Renewal costs associated with the CAPEX scheme (2), as an Estimator I need the software to apply the relevant unit rates for each renewal activity. In addition to these unit rates, the software will apply a top down adjustment for Prelims, TTM, Design, SU, Other costs and Fee.
1193.acceptanceCriteria: As an estimator, I can use quantities produced for a CAPEX scheme to Inform the Asset Renewals estimate within a whole lifecycle cost and carbon estimate.

1210.description: Based on the value of the work packages for each Supplier the software should apply the relevant Fee. The methodology when the Supplier is Unknown could utilise the logic from the current SDF pricing workbooks.
1210.acceptanceCriteria:
• As an estimator, I can apply relevant fees from the Supplier Fee Library to work packages based on their value.

• As an estimator, I can apply fees from the Supplier Fee Library when the supplier is unknown, using configured thresholds, e.g. to align with the current SDF pricing workbooks’ logic.

1220.description: For long term (whole life) asset renewals estimates, the quantity of item works in a given year will be calculated from the quantity of assets to be renewed and the asset renewal frequency. The estimator will want the ability to overwrite these default quantities with a specific quantity.
1220.acceptanceCriteria:
• A User can specify the OMR assessment period from 1-200 years

• A User can specify the Asset Quantity, % of asset to be renewed at each intervention and Renewal Frequency (i.e. lifespan of the Asset) for each Segment within the Asset Renewal estimate
