When an IFT revision / forecast has been rejected by a Reviewer, the forecast is no longer locked and can then be edited by the Project User.

2500.description: Access controls so that Contractors can only see relevant dashboards
2500.acceptanceCriteria: An Administrator can configure administration settings that control Project User access to CCET dashboards and reports.

2510.description: Contractors should be able to select a scheme and the appropriate lifecycle stage and select the client carbon estimate to view
2510.acceptanceCriteria: An administrator can control the level of carbon data from NH estimates that is visible as a baseline for supplier forecasts in the CCET. A Project User can see this level of carbon data for the projects and life cycle stage to which they have access permissions. (It is anticipated that carbon rates and totals for all Resources and Items will be visible in the baseline.)

2520.description: For the PCF Stage 0-2 Forecast, no rates should be visible to the Forecast project team user
2520.acceptanceCriteria:
An administrator can control the level of cost data from NH estimates that is visible as a baseline for supplier forecasts in the CCET. The administrator sets this control across the CCET in a table within the administration settings.

The administrator can select one of the following whether forecast baselines' rate and cost columns are visible at the following levels: 
- None (no baseline cost data is visible to Project Users) 
- Project (only baseline Project cost totals are visible to Project Users) 
- Section (only baseline Section and Project cost totals are visible to Project Users) 
- Item (baseline Item rates, Item costs, Section and Project cost totals are visible to Project Users)  
- Resource (all rates and costs in the baseline are visible to Project Users)

2530.description:
The Forecast reviewer should only have "read-only" access. At the same point in time, the contractor estimator should be able to edit the estimate while it is under review - this is so that changes and improvement can be done to the estimate by the contractor

The IFT reviewer should only have "read-only" access. At the same point in time, the contractor estimator should be able to edit the estimate while it is under review - this is so that changes and improvement can be done to the estimate by the contractor
2530.acceptanceCriteria:
The NH reviewer of an IFT revision / forecast submission has read-only access to the IFT revision / forecast and cannot edit the IFT revision / forecast with the exception of Review status and comments fields.

Once an IFT revision / forecast is submitted for review, the IFT revision / forecast is locked and cannot be edited.

A Project User, who wishes to make changes to an IFT revision / submitted forecast, Project User can duplicate the IFT revision / submission forecast, increasing the revision number (see FR 1560) and edit the new IFT revision.

When an IFT revision / forecast has been rejected by a Reviewer, the IFT revision / submission forecast is no longer locked and can then be edited by the Project User.

2540.description: Varying levels of control in the system to show the section level costs, or not show costs at all - across all estimates
2540.acceptanceCriteria: An administrator can control the level of cost data from NH estimates that is visible as a baseline for supplier forecasts in the CCET. The administrator sets this control across the CCET in a table within the administration settings.

2550.description: Estimator-level Access Controls for B2-B5 carbon assumptions
2550.acceptanceCriteria: The CCET contains an administrator setting that controls whether estimators may edit library default carbon values or calculations for nested modules for PAS 2080 Stage B modules

2560.description: System should have permissions to control which Estimators can manually enter carbon factors
2560.acceptanceCriteria: The CCET contains an administrator setting that controls whether estimators may delink resources and edit carbon values from the carbon library used for the NH carbon estimate.

2570.description: The inflation index should be estimate-specific and the inflation indices used in the estimate must be stored with an Authorised and Completed estimate so that the user can identify which inflation profile was used
2570.acceptanceCriteria: When an estimate is 'Authorised', the inflation factors (from estimate base date to estimated time of expenditure) for each cost element will be 'locked' and will not be editable.

2580.description: The system should have relevant controls to assign authority to users to review and approve Contractor's estimate
2580.acceptanceCriteria: An CCET Administrator sets NH User permissions for reviewers to enable review and approval of IFT revision / submitted forecasts.

2590.description: Configurable application branding - "National Highways estimating tool" (this will need to be configurable by user and allow a logo to be added)
2590.acceptanceCriteria: The National Highways chosen name for the CCET will be provided on every principal screen, dashboard and report of the CCET.

2600.description: Ensure consistent terminology within both Carbon Tool and Benchmark application
2600.acceptanceCriteria: Benchmark carbon estimating functionality will use the same terminology as Benchmark cost estimating functionality for when describing the same data field, data structure element, function or operation.

2610.description: Standardised language across the system that aligns with the British standard for LCC - 15686/5
2610.acceptanceCriteria: The Terminology in the CCET will be consistent with Chapter 8 of BS ISO 15686-5, Standardized Method of Life Cycle Costing for Construction Procurement: 'Terms, Definitions and Abbreviations'

2620.description: Standardised naming convention for Schemes and Estimates
2620.acceptanceCriteria: Administrators can configure and edit a library of ‘Estimate Output Types’ that contains the Estimate Type's Name and the lifecycle stages which the Estimate Shell covers for a selected Estimate Output Type. (See FR20.)

2630.description: The terminology for Lifecycle Stages must be consistent - Construction, Operation & Maintenance, Renewal and Decommissioning
2630.acceptanceCriteria: The naming of Lifecyle costing stages is standardised in the CCET and aligns with the BS ISO 15686-5, Standardized Method of Life Cycle Costing for Construction Procurement: 'Terms, Definitions and Abbreviations'

2650.description: Enhanced user navigation and clear, consistent screen titles
2650.acceptanceCriteria: Each CCET screen in the CCET has a clear title.

2660.description:
Estimating Manager view - Ability to easily access graphs/visuals of an estimate to understand and review the proposed estimate. Minimum are below:
- CESS
- CERT
- RET
- other estimate outputs / reports
2660.acceptanceCriteria:
• ‘Dashboards’ or graphical reports displayed on screen for the cost & carbon estimate to show the following for each estimate type:
  • A cost / carbon estimate summary at Section, Cost element and resource level , showing base estimate at Section level, project and portfolio risk/opportunity/uncertainty allowances and inflation covering individual or all lifecycle stages. For carbon information is displayed compliant to PAS 2080 Modules
  • A summary of the estimated costs /carbon over time, broken down by Cost element and resource level , base estimate, project risk, portfolio risk and inflation allowances for each financial year
  • A summary of estimated costs for net present value calculations at an administrator-controlled price base, which:
      • can be configured to exclude spend to date and taxation
      • presents costs with and without portfolio risk allowances
   • A summary of the cost estimate showing range minimum, most-likely, maximum and each 10th percentile interval for probabilistic estimates
• Dashboards shows the project name, estimate title, estimate type, and estimate ID reference
• Dashboards displays the price base of the cost data prior to application of inflation allowances
• Dashboards can be exported to MS Excel and PDF
• The data displays identical numbers to the estimate database

2670.description:
Estimator view - Ability to easily access graphs/visuals of an estimate to prepare the final estimate outputs:
- CESS
- CERT
- RET
- other estimate outputs / reports

2680.description: As an estimator and estimating manager, I want to easily view all the estimates produced for a scheme in chronological order to see the evolution of the estimated costs, and carbon. I also want to be able to select and deselect individual estimates from this chart / table, for all estimate types as set out in Scope Table A.
2680.acceptanceCriteria:
• A user can generate a report showing the evolution of the estimated cost and carbon for a scheme, by selecting the selective or all approved estimates to include in the report. The report will display:
   • The estimates in chronological order
   • The estimate ID and date
   • The estimate classification

2700.description: Filter Cost and Carbon Estimates by Portfolio, Programme, Scheme, Estimate Name and Estimate ID - See FR above
2700.acceptanceCriteria: The CCET contains an Estimate Browser which shows all Estimates in the CCET, subject to the permissions of the NH Estimator to view estimates.

2710.description: Navigation around the system for a user must be clear and efficient. It should be very clear where a user is within the overall system on each screen and be able to quickly go back to "home" screens.
2710.acceptanceCriteria: Each CCET screen in the CCET has a clear title.

2730.description: The software should have efficient number of "clicks" to be able to edit / enter data into fields.
2730.acceptanceCriteria: Users can edit data fields efficiently with an appropriate number of 'clicks' to edit data fields.

2740.description: The hierarchy and items and resources within an estimate should be clearly indented / colour-coded to identify the level of the hierarchy that each line belongs to.
2740.acceptanceCriteria:
The WBS levels in an estimate are clearly identified to Users. There is distinct formatting (e.g. shading and / or font) and / or indenting for each of the following levels: 
- Section 
- Cost Element 
- Item 
- Resource

2760.description: Screens should be well laid out with appropriate space allocated to rows and columns so that users have minimal scrolling re-allocating width / depth to columns / rows. Toggles should provide the ability to hide / display columns and fields from screens / reports, where these are not relevant to the specific client.
2760.acceptanceCriteria: Toggles (to hide / show columns) and / or collapsing / expanding rows and columns are provided for estimate CCET BoQ, 'CESS', and Estimate Summary screens covering base estimate risk and inflation. This is a substantial amount of the estimate build-up can be shown on one screen without scrolling.

1530.1.description: As an estimator, I need to produce TOTEX cost estimates that show estimated costs with and without discounting, and with / without relative price growth and the option to apply market adjustment factors or not.  The discount factors and relative price growth factors applied in the estimate should be clearly presented to users and in reports.
1530.1.acceptanceCriteria: The CCET stores a library of default discount rates for application to estimates and calculation of net present value.
